text:
sophie: Heads-up: we're seeing intermittent dropped pod connections in us-west2 GPU pool starting ~06:20 UTC, seems east-west path only. Pods report TCP resets and liveness probes failing -> restarts.

tom: saw that. Any conntrack + ephemeral port errors in dmesg?

sophie: grabbing logs now. early signs point at conntrack saturation on the node egress NAT—kube-proxy is in iptables mode.

sophie: paste from node-gn-12: 
```
# conntrack -S | grep entries
parms: 
entries: 65536
used: 65499
found: 129

# cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
65536
# ss -s | grep estab
TCP: 
  12345 established
```

raj: whoa used 65499/65536, that's dangerously close. are these mostly ephemeral OUT connections? can you `conntrack -L | awk '{print $6}' | cut -d= -f2 | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head` ?

sophie: ran quick sample, majority are `ESTABLISHED src=10.32.x.x:random_port dst=10.128.y.y:443`, so pod->pod or pod->service flows hitting SNAT on node.

julie: are we using hairpin SNAT for traffic to node-local services? recall a change last week where we toggled `externalTrafficPolicy` on some services.

sophie: some model-prefetch sidecars call internal control endpoints via node IP; hairpin paths get SNAT'd. also see lots of short lived connections from model loader processes - high churn.

infra-bot: deploy/rollout detected: model-prefetch v2 rolled to us-west2 at 05:58 UTC.

tom: that explains spike correlation. High connection churn + SNAT per flow = conntrack blowout. we should either reduce SNAT paths or bump nf_conntrack_max and tune timeouts.

raj: bumping nf_conntrack_max helps but is temporary. need to reduce per-flow count: enable endpoint slices, move sidecars to use clusterIP DNS (no SNAT) or enable `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` where applicable. Also consider conntrack hashsize and net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established reduction? careful with healthy long-lived grpc.

sophie: we tried lowering `tcp_timeout_established` to 6h already; most flows are <10s. current conntrack entries have timeout ~30s for many.

julie: can we route internal control plane traffic over pod IPs (disable node port access) so it never SNATs? That would require changing how prefetcher resolves service endpoints.

ops-oncall: temporary mitigation: increased nf_conntrack_max from 65536 -> 196608 on nodes in us-west2, and added a conntrack sweeper cron to prune TIME_WAIT older than 60s. watching metrics.

sophie: after bump, used dropped from 65499 -> 72000 used. immediate pod restarts stopped. need long-term fix.

tom: follow-ups: (1) rollback/patch prefetcher to use cluster IPs (2) audit services using node IP / hostPort / hostNetwork (3) evaluate kube-proxy ipvs to avoid massive iptables conntrack hits (4) consider enabling kubelet `--hairpin-mode=none` for affected pods.

raj: also audit MTU/RDMA path: any evidence of fragmentation/ICMP blackhole causing lots of small retransmissions? RDMA flows should be on separate NICs but double-check.

sophie: I ran `dmesg` and `ethtool -S` on a sample node; no obvious MTU drops, RDMA counters normal. Packet loss on fabric reported ~0.01% during spike. not enough to explain churn.

julie: cost note: bumping conntrack_max increases memory per node (~24 bytes/entry). at 200k entries that's ~5MB, negligible for our GPU nodes. but we must avoid permanent overprovision.

ops-oncall: created incident ticket INF-3841: "us-west2 conntrack exhaustion causing pod restarts" and scheduled 2hr postmortem.

sophie: adding checklist to ticket: node sysctl deploy, prefetcher code change PR, kube-proxy ipvs test, monitoring alert refinements (conntrack usage % -> warn at 60% critical 85%).

tom: quick test idea: run a synthetic churner to reproduce on staging: 2000 ephemeral connections/s between pods with node SNAT to see how conntrack behaves. I'll own the test infra.

raj: thanks. if test reproduces, we should also confirm conntrack GC tunables: `nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait` and `nf_conntrack_generic_timeout` for UDP.

sophie: okay folks, I'm going to keep monitoring. ping me if you want access to node-gn-12 logs. :raised_hands: 

infra-bot: alert: conntrack usage us-west2 > 80% (3 nodes).

ops-oncall: scaling plan: add 4 spare nodes to the GPU pool for capacity while we implement code changes.

julie: jotting down follow-ups in the ticket, assigning ownership. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
